detector.model: google/owlv2-base-patch16-ensemble at revision cfd3195ba4ea9592eec887ded089f4c08eff231d, CPU, each query scored on its own (sigmoid of its logit)
detector.score_cut_rule: Run the detector on candidate 1 of the source of each of the ten main scenes (SA01 to SA10) with two kinds of query. Present: the scene's rearrangement-object queries (19 in all; SA06 has one query, 'an oar'). Absent: eight objects that cannot appear in a scene plausible for 1900 to 1925 (a smartphone; a laptop computer; a television set; a computer keyboard; a plastic water bottle; a jet airplane; a satellite dish; a microwave oven), the same eight for every scene (80 in all). Each query's score is its best box's score. Every observed score is a possible cut c; Youden's J(c) is the share of present scores at or above c minus the share of absent scores at or above c. c* is the smallest observed score with the largest J. The score cut is the midpoint between c* and the largest observed score below c*, rounded to three decimals. A detection counts when its score is at least the cut.
detector.distinct_boxes_rule: Two boxes for one query are the same object when their IoU is at least 0.5 (fixed, not set from data).

change_mask.difference: Per-pixel difference d: the Euclidean distance between the two images' RGB values (0 to 441), with no smoothing.
change_mask.difference_threshold_rule: Over every pixel of candidate 1 of the small and of the medium addition of each of the ten main scenes (20 raw edits, each compared with the source it was made from), take the median m and the median absolute deviation MAD of d. The threshold is m + 3.5 x MAD / 0.6745, the value at which a pixel's modified z-score (Iglewicz and Hoaglin, 1993) passes 3.5, rounded to one decimal. A pixel is marked as changed when d is above the threshold.
change_mask.speck_rule: With that threshold, find every 8-connected group of marked pixels in the same 20 edits. The speck size is the 99.9th percentile of the groups' sizes in pixels, rounded up to a whole number. Every group of at most that many pixels is a speck and is removed; then every unmarked area wholly enclosed by marked pixels is filled. The result is the cleaned change mask.
change_mask.widening_rule: With the cleaned change masks of the same 20 edits, for each whole-pixel distance k = 1, 2, ... from the mask (Euclidean distance), take the median of d over the pixels whose distance lies in (k - 1, k], pooled over the 20 edits. The widening radius is the smallest k whose ring median is at most m, the median of d over all pixels (the level of the model's re-rendering of an unchanged pixel), so the edge of the pasted region falls where the edit differs from its input no more than a typical pixel does. If no k up to 64 qualifies, the radius is 64.
change_mask.widened_mask: Every pixel within the widening radius of the cleaned mask (Euclidean distance), with enclosed holes filled.
change_mask.compositing: The accepted file takes the raw edit's pixels inside the widened mask and the input's pixels everywhere else (input = the accepted source for small and medium; the accepted, composited medium file for large).
change_mask.masked_area: Share of the image (percent of 1536 x 1024 pixels) inside the cleaned change mask of the composited file compared with the accepted source, computed with the same threshold and cleaning. For the large file this includes the medium element.

Size, by within-scene ordering of the masked area (above): small at least 0.1 percent of the image; medium at least 2 times the accepted small file's masked area for the scene and at least 0.5 percent; large at least 2 times the accepted medium file's masked area. acceptance.description_model: gpt-5.1-2025-11-13, reasoning effort none, temperature 0, at most 16 output tokens, one question per call with the instruction 'Look at the image and answer the question with exactly one word: yes or no.'; the reply must be exactly yes or no (case, spaces and a final full stop ignored); other replies are asked again, three calls at most, then recorded as invalid, which does not confirm.
acceptance.order: Candidates are numbered in the order made, per scene and file; the first that passes every check is accepted and no later candidate is judged.

rescue.count: The 20 tries are counted per scene and per file (source, small, medium, large); only requests that return an image count as tries.
rescue.source_revision: After 20 failed source candidates, one revision: the bank's eight sentences, then the sentence 'Make sure the image clearly shows ' + the items whose check failed in more than half of the 20 tries (objects named by their detector query, the open area by the scene's open-area phrase), joined with commas and 'and', + '.', then the closing sentence. The candidate count restarts at the next number; 20 more tries.
rescue.addition_revision: After 20 failed candidates of an addition, one revision: 'Add ' + phrase + ', clearly visible. Change nothing else.' (for large, the phrase is the two further elements). 20 more tries.
rescue.reserve: A scene with no passing candidate for any of its four files after the revision is replaced by the reserve of its kind (SA-R1 for a scene with a person, SA-R2 without), which takes its place in every A1 list; the reserve's four files are made by the same rules.

basis.units: percent of the image's 1536 x 1024 pixels

amendments.what: New acceptance condition for every Set A addition: the 'unchanged elsewhere' check
amendments.decided_by: David G. Kamper, 28 October 2026, before any participant data
amendments.rule: The description model (gpt-5.1-2025-11-13, reasoning off, temperature 0, at most 16 output tokens) is shown the edit's input and the composited file in one request: the text 'First image:', the input, the text 'Second image:', the composited file, then the instruction 'Look at the two images and answer the question with exactly one word: yes or no.' and 'Question: Apart from <the added element or elements, named as in the instruction>, is everything that was in the first image still in the same place and unchanged in the second image?'. For large the input is the accepted medium file and the question names the medium element and the two further elements. The answer must be 'yes'; any other reply is asked again, three calls at most, then recorded as invalid, which does not confirm. The question is asked only of a candidate that passes every earlier check.
amendments.reason: A1 tells participants that Alex 'changed nothing else'. Two accepted large files (SA04, whose edit also redrew the empty chair, and SA-R1, whose edit moved the framed picture) changed existing objects inside the pasted region and still passed every earlier check.
amendments.consequences: Every Set A addition in use is re-judged in candidate order: the question is asked of the earliest candidate that passes every earlier check; on 'no' the search continues in order through the candidates that passed the earlier checks, then with new candidates under the rescue rule. When a small file changes, its medium's size minimum (2 x small) changes with it; when a medium changes, large candidates made from the old medium are superseded and the large is searched again from the new medium. The earlier judgments are kept in each record under previous_judgments. The replaced scenes SA05 and SA08 are not re-judged, since their files are not used.

amendments.what: Spill check replaces the 'unchanged elsewhere' description question for every Set A addition
amendments.decided_by: David G. Kamper, 28 October 2026, before any participant data
amendments.supersedes: the 'unchanged elsewhere' question of the amendment above; its answers stay in each candidate's previous_judgments and in manifest.csv
amendments.rule: Added-element region: for each element the file must show (small: the small element; medium: the medium element; large: the medium element and the two further elements), every detector box for the element's query that scores at least the detector score cut and whose center lies inside the composited region (the widened mask; for large, the union of the medium's and the large's widened masks), each box's rectangle grown by the widening radius (64 pixels) on every side and clipped to the image; the region is the union of these rectangles. Spill: the percent of the image's 1536 x 1024 pixels that lie inside the cleaned change mask (before widening; the edit's input against the composited file, with the frozen difference threshold and speck rule) but outside the added-element region. Cut: compute spill for candidate 1 of every addition file that has one (small, medium and large across all twelve scenes, reserves included), each rebuilt from its raw edit and its input with the frozen thresholds; the cut is median + 3.5 x MAD / 0.6745 of those values, rounded up to three decimals (numbers.spill_cut_pct). A file passes when its spill is at or below the cut.
amendments.readings_made_determinate: 'The detector's accepted boxes' is read as every box that confirms the element (score at least the cut, center inside the composited region), so that plural elements (a stack of barrels, a row of lanterns, buckets of flowers, reeds) are covered by all their boxes; 'widened by 64 pixels' is read as growing each box's rectangle by 64 pixels on every side.
amendments.reason: The two-image description question answered 'yes' for SA04 large c28 (the edit redrew the empty chair) and SA-R1 large c42 (the edit moved the framed picture), the two known cases it was meant to catch.
amendments.consequences: Every addition in use is re-judged in candidate order under all current checks with the spill check in place of the question; when a medium changes, its large is searched again; searches continue under the rescue rule.

amendments.what: Object-position check replaces the spill check for every Set A addition
amendments.decided_by: David G. Kamper, 29 October 2026, before any participant data
amendments.supersedes: the spill check of 28 October 2026; its values stay in each candidate's previous_judgments and in manifest.csv
amendments.rule: Tracked objects (fixed per scene before any judging, in tracked_objects): the noun chunks (spaCy 3.7.4, en_core_web_sm 3.7.1) of the scene's Composition and Background sentences in the bank; each chunk's head noun as the detector query 'a' or 'an' + noun; excluded: the scene's added elements at all three amounts, the person or people of the Subject sentence, and the surfaces and regions area, background, center, centre, corner, distance, end, field, floor, foreground, frame, ground, horizon, left, right, river, road, room, rug, sea, side, sky, street, stretch, table, third, wall, water. A tracked object is trackable when the detector finds it in the accepted source at or above the score cut; otherwise it is untrackable and ignored. A file passes when every trackable object found in its input (at or above the cut) is also found in the composited file, at or above the cut, by a box whose intersection over union with the object's box in the input is at least 0.5 (a fixed constant, not tuned); for each object the best-matching box is used. The input is the source for small and medium, and the accepted medium for large.
amendments.readings_made_determinate: Head noun: the chunk's root token when it is a noun, lemmatized to the singular ('oars' -> 'an oar'); chunks whose root is a pronoun ('She', 'his right') are skipped. 'an' before a vowel letter, else 'a'. Added elements: the head noun of each element phrase's first noun chunk and the noun (last word, and its singular) of the element's detector query, for the small, medium and large phrases in use. Person: the head noun of the Subject sentence's first noun chunk, in a scene with a person. The object's box in the input: its best-scoring box at or above the cut; an object not found in a file's input is not checked for that file. The lists are the rule's literal output and include chunk heads that are not objects ('a hand', 'a band', 'a front', 'a glow'); they are applied as written.
amendments.reason: The spill check measures pixel change: it penalized re-rendered texture (SA-R2's hay) and passed a moved object of modest size (SA04's chair). A1's statement promises that no existing object moved or vanished, which this check tests directly.
amendments.consequences: Every addition in use is re-judged in candidate order under all current checks with the object-position check in place of the spill check, starting with SA-R2 small's existing candidates; when a medium changes, its large is searched again; searches continue under the rescue rule.
